skill.name: prpm-json-best-practices
skill.description: Guidance for creating and maintaining prpm.json package manifests, including required metadata, collections, tags, files, validation, and publishing workflows.
skill.summary: Create clean PRPM manifests for packages, collections, validation, activation settings, and publishing workflows.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: I found no malicious intent, prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden runtime behavior in the reviewed files. The static findings are documentation, schema metadata, placeholder examples, and local command examples rather than executable skill code. Lifecycle script examples should still be reviewed before use, but they are presented as normal publishing guidance.

| `category`    | string   | Recommended | Collection category (development, testing, etc.)       |
| `icon`        | string   | Optional    | Emoji or icon (max 10 chars)                           |

content.value_statement: PRPM package manifests can become inconsistent across packages, collections, and supported AI tools. This skill gives structured guidance for complete, valid, and maintainable prpm.json files.
actual_capabilities: Explains required fields for single-package and multi-package prpm.json manifests.
Shows how to define collections that reference packages by packageId.
Documents valid format and subtype values for PRPM packages.
Guides eager and lazy activation settings for skills and agents.
Covers tags, naming, versioning, file paths, duplicate checks, and validation steps.
Describes prepublishOnly lifecycle scripts for build tasks before publishing.
limitations: It does not validate manifests by itself without a separate JSON validator or PRPM command.
It focuses on PRPM package manifests, not general package manager configuration.
It cannot confirm that referenced package files exist unless the agent inspects the repository.
It does not replace security review for lifecycle scripts or package contents.

use_cases.title: Create a first PRPM package
use_cases.description: Use the field guidance to prepare a complete manifest for one Claude, Cursor, or generic package.

use_cases.title: Organize a multi-package repository
use_cases.description: Define package entries, names, versions, tags, files, privacy settings, and consistent metadata in one manifest.

use_cases.title: Review package collections
use_cases.description: Check collection entries for package identifiers, version ranges, required flags, reasons, categories, and searchable tags.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a basic manifest
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prpm.json plan for one Claude skill. Include required fields, recommended tags, file paths, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review an existing manifest
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my prpm.json for missing required fields, duplicate names, weak tags, invalid file paths, and publishing risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a multi-package repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Help organize a multi-package prpm.json. Group packages by privacy, format, and subtype, then suggest naming and versioning improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan collections and conversion hints
prompt_templates.prompt: Design PRPM collections and conversion hints for packages that target Claude, Cursor, Continue, Windsurf, Copilot, Kiro, and Agents.md.

output_examples.input: I need a manifest for one Claude skill.
output_examples.output: A concise manifest plan with required metadata, package type, file path guidance, tags, and a validation checklist.

output_examples.input: My repository publishes several related prompt packages.
output_examples.output: An organization plan that groups private packages first, separates formats, aligns versions, and highlights duplicate-name risks.

output_examples.input: I want to bundle existing packages into a collection.
output_examples.output: A collection design with package identifiers, version ranges, required flags, reasons, categories, and searchable tags.

best_practices: Keep prpm.json for packages you publish, and keep installed dependencies in prpm.lock.
Use specific kebab-case tags that describe technology, domain, and purpose.
Validate required fields, duplicate names, file paths, and versions before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not copy installed packages from prpm.lock into prpm.json.
Do not use absolute file paths in package file lists.
Do not use prepublish scripts that also run during package installation.

faq.question: When should I use prpm.json?
faq.answer: Use it when publishing your own PRPM packages, collections, skills, agents, rules, prompts, or related package metadata.

faq.question: Does this skill create valid JSON automatically?
faq.answer: It guides the structure and checks to perform. A validator or PRPM command should still confirm final syntax and schema compliance.

faq.question: Can it help with multi-package repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains package arrays, naming, grouping, duplicate checks, privacy settings, files, versions, and shared repository metadata.

faq.question: Does it support PRPM collections?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents collection fields, package references, version ranges, required packages, optional packages, reasons, and categories.

faq.question: What AI tools are covered?
faq.answer: The guidance references formats such as Claude, Cursor, Continue, Windsurf, Copilot, Kiro, Agents.md, generic packages, and MCP.

faq.question: Should lifecycle scripts be reviewed?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends prepublishOnly for build tasks, but every command should be reviewed before it runs.
